questions.q: Which four personality types does Erikson build the book around?
a: Red, yellow, green and blue
Red, blue, white and black
Fire, air, water and earth
Dominant, steady, cautious and inspiring
questions.why: Lesson 1 maps the four types to the old choleric, sanguine, phlegmatic and melancholic categories.

questions.q: Which type is calm, easygoing, loyal and quick to avoid conflict?
a: Green
Red
Yellow
Blue
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes the Green type as a great listener and team player who dislikes conflict.

questions.q: Which personality type is the most common in the world?
a: Green, the calm and loyal type
Red, the ambitious and competitive type
Yellow, the cheerful and social type
Blue, the analytical perfectionist
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Green is the most widespread type, which is why they seem so friendly and easy to be around.

questions.q: How should you give feedback to a Red, or choleric, person?
a: Lead with strong arguments and skip the small talk
Bring a written list and repeat it later
Meet privately and expect a slow response
Walk through every detail step by step
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Reds dislike chatting around and want you to get straight to the point.

questions.q: How should you deliver criticism to a Blue, or melancholic, person?
a: Be very detailed and be ready for their questions
Get straight to the point with no preamble
Offer a short list and allow plenty of time
Keep it light and informal throughout
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Blues accept feedback when you show them each step and answer their questions.
